title: No non-closed point in the distinguished fibre
statement: Let S be a scheme, Ω an algebraically closed field, s : Spec Ω → S a geometric point, A a commutative local ring, and e : Spec A ≅ S_(s), where S_(s) is [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and its structural map ρ_s is [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. For every x in Spec A, if ρ_s(e(x)) = s(closedPoint Ω), then x = closedPoint A.

proof.text: Choose an affine open chart containing s(closedPoint Ω) and factor the geometric point through it. The spectrum of Ω is a singleton, so its entire image lies in this chart. Apply the chart maximal-ideal theorem and transport its existential conclusion along the factorization equality to obtain a local coordinate ring C and ρ : R → C with Spec(ρ) ≫ i = the structural map and maximalIdeal(C) = p.map(ρ).

The assumed structural-image equality, together with injectivity of the open immersion i, says the prime of e(x) contracts under ρ to p. By Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap its ideal contains p.map(ρ) = maximalIdeal(C). Conversely every prime ideal in a local ring is contained in its maximal ideal. Antisymmetry and PrimeSpectrum.ext imply e(x) is the closed point of Spec C.

Every point in Spec C specializes to its closed point. Every point in Spec A specializes to its closed point, so applying e to the specialization of e.inv(closedPoint C) gives a specialization from closedPoint C to e(closedPoint A). The inverse identity and T0 antisymmetry show e(closedPoint A) = closedPoint C. Injectivity of e then gives x = closedPoint A.

theorem strictHenselizationStructuralMap_fiber_eq_closedPoint_of_eq
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {Ω A : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (e : Spec (.of A) ≅ strictHenselizationScheme s)
    (x : Spec (.of A))
    (h : (e.hom ≫ strictHenselizationStructuralMap s) x =
      s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω)) :
    x = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A
